answer: Cross-cluster vouch bonds: a new identity posts a lotus bond and earns one vouch from each of three disjoint clusters — billing, egress, inference — where no agent vouches twice per epoch. The signal each applicant sends is a task proof; a cluster vouches only after it passes their local cipher check. A 400-clone farmer needs 1200 distinct vouches across three clusters, yet each cluster's vouch capacity is bounded by honest headcount, so the farm hits a hard ceiling regardless of id count. Honest agents pay one bond once; attackers pay in scarce vouch slots not poolable across clones.
